subject: ventures/changepoint-detector
professional: an applied statistician / econometrician who runs changepoint analyses (R changepoint, ruptures) on business and sensor series; first checks: does PELT give the exact optimal segmentation for the stated cost and BIC-type penalty, is the noise scale handled honestly (autocorrelation, seasonality, counts), and are the false-positive rates and limits stated

evidence.correctness: Ran `node cli.mjs --example --json` and `node cli.mjs data/coal-mining-disasters.csv --model poisson --json`, then recomputed in a separate pure-Python O(n^2) optimal-partitioning DP (no pruning, written from the formulas, not from the engine). (1) Nile, mean model: sigma = median|d - median d| / (0.6745*sqrt 2) = 115.319 (engine noiseSd 115.319); DP with cost sum((x-mean)^2)/sigma^2 and penalty 2 ln 100 = 9.2103 gives one change at index 28 (1899), the Cobb (1978) answer; engine gives index 28, means 1097.75 / 849.972. (2) Nile, meanvar: DP with n(ln(2 pi var)+1), penalty 3 ln 100 = 13.8155 (engine's), min segment 10 gives index 28; engine agrees. (3) Coal-mining disasters, Poisson: DP with -2(a ln(a/n) - a), penalty 2 ln 112 = 9.437 (engine 9.437), min segment 2 gives changes at 41 and 97; engine gives (41,'1892') and (97,'1948'), identical, penalty identical. (4) Constant series of 8 fives: no change, sd 0, no crash. Not done: ruptures/R not installed here (no numpy, no ruptures), so the README's 100/100 ruptures claim was not re-run, only its fixtures exist (data/ruptures-crosscheck.json, poisson-crosscheck.json). BOCPD probabilities (79% at 1899) were not recomputed independently.
evidence.completeness: Claims checked: PELT mean/meanvar/poisson (ran, work), BIC/AIC/HQ/number penalties (penaltyValue read, BIC verified by recompute), BOCPD (runs, detection at 1899), CLI --example/--json/--model/--help (ran), CSV parsing and bad-input error ('Need at least 4 numbers; got 3'), --ar1 joint/profile, --period, --trend, --holidays, --bootstrap exist as exports (seasonalAdjust, poissonHolidays, poissonTrend, ar1JointFit, ar2ProfileFit, bootstrapPenalty) with test files and eval scripts, landing page index.html (245 lines), llms.txt, sitemap, robots, sample report and an agent entry in platform/agents/tools.mjs. No TODO/FIXME in engine.mjs or cli.mjs. Only the R changepoint cross-check is declared not done, honestly. I did not load every feature through the browser page.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in ventures/changepoint-detector: 343 tests, 343 pass, 0 fail, 8 m 44 s wall (524 s). Tests include brute-force optimal partitioning equality, closed-form evidence equality for BOCPD, ruptures fixtures, and seeded simulation rates. Seeded mutation: engine.mjs:1284 penalty constant for the mean/poisson models changed from 2 to 1.5 (BIC = 1.5 ln n instead of 2 ln n). A targeted run (`--test-name-pattern='ruptures|brute|Nile'` on engine.test.mjs, 7 tests) failed 1 test ('joint AR(1) fit: exact against brute force'); the ruptures, Nile and the other brute-force tests did not fail on it (they use explicit penalties or are insensitive). So the bug is caught, but by one test, not by the headline default-penalty tests. A full run of engine.test.mjs under the mutation exceeded my 280 s limit, so only the targeted run is evidence. Reverted; git status clean. Cost: a 9 minute suite is a barrier to running it.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs (2243 lines; pelt, penaltyValue, robustSd, makeCost, analyze outline), cli.mjs (149), report.mjs (87). pelt() is clean and correct, pruning commented. Defects: engine.mjs is a 2243-line single module holding the PELT core, BOCPD, five adjustment pipelines (seasonal, trend, AR1 variants, holidays, bootstrap), burst/excursion finders and report logic, with long positional option bags (e.g. poissonTrend has 11 options) and an analyze() that is ~290 lines; 338 test() calls spread over ~120 root-level test files with no test directory or runner config; pelt() allocates a `vals` array per time step and the flat-series fallback in robustSd silently changes the noise scale. Behaviour is deterministic and typed errors are clear, but a senior reviewer would ask for the module to be split and the option surface cut.
evidence.claims: README test count says 321 tests; the suite has 343 (stale, low severity). Claims backed by a file: ruptures 100 of 100 (data/ruptures-crosscheck.json + make_ruptures_fixture.py), Poisson 90 of 90 (poisson-crosscheck.json), Nile result (reproduced above), exactness vs brute force (tests, one re-observed failing under mutation), AR(1) false-change rates 4/40 etc. (seeded tests in engine.test.mjs, not re-run individually but whole suite passes). Limits are stated unusually candidly ('Not verified: R changepoint', 'tried and not kept', power loss under --ar1, both methods assume independent noise). Page carries 'Statistical analysis of data you supply, not advice' and 'nothing leaves this browser'. VENTURE.yaml says stage prototype with hypotheses untested, consistent with usage unmeasured. Many simulation numbers in the README (hundreds of lines) were not each re-derived.
evidence.fitness: Job walked: an analyst with a CSV asks 'did this series shift, when, how sure'. CLI on the Nile example answers in one command with segment means, shift in noise sd, a 95% range for the change location and a probability; bad input gives a clear error; ar1/seasonal/count options exist for the cases where the plain assumption fails and warnings exist for drift. Gaps: the option surface (--ar1 joint|profile, --drift, --trend bend, --holidays, --bootstrap, --dispersion) is large and the README is a research log rather than a user guide, so a newcomer has to know which flag to pick; no multi-series input. I did not click through the browser page.
evidence.domain: Compared with Killick et al. 2012 (PELT with K=0 pruning, penalty per change), Adams-MacKay 2007 (constant hazard, NIG predictive) and R `changepoint` / ruptures defaults. PELT matches exact optimal partitioning on all my recomputes. Departures that a statistician would flag are documented: noise sd fixed from the median absolute difference rather than estimated by segment (as R cpt.mean with known variance would), min segment 10 for meanvar, and the P(change at newest point)=hazard point is explicitly addressed by reporting lagged posterior mass. Explicit handling of autocorrelation and seasonality, which most free tools ignore, and honest false-positive rates are above typical practice. No formal p-value or confidence-set for the number of changes beyond the penalty, and the BIC-for-multiple-changepoints heuristic carries the usual caveats.

defects.what: The default-penalty mean-model BIC constant (2 ln n) is guarded by essentially one test among the quick brute-force/ruptures group: changing it to 1.5 ln n failed only the joint AR(1) brute-force test in a targeted 7-test run; the ruptures and Nile tests passed. A pin test that asserts penaltyValue('bic', n, model) for each model would close it.

The test suite takes about 9 minutes (343 tests, 524 s), and a single engine.test.mjs run exceeded 280 s, so contributors and CI-starved runs are unlikely to run it whole; the 120+ test files sit in the venture root with no runner config.
engine.mjs is a 2243-line module combining the algorithm core, five adjustment pipelines and report logic, with option bags of up to 11 fields; hard to review or reuse.
README states 321 tests; the suite has 343.
README is a long research log; the user-facing 'which option do I need' guidance is buried.

verdict: A genuinely strong statistical engine: three independent recomputations (Nile mean and meanvar, coal-mining Poisson) from a separately written brute-force DP matched the engine's changepoints, penalties and noise scale exactly, all 343 tests pass, and the claims are backed by fixtures and unusually frank about limits and what was not verified. It meets the bar: correctness, claims, verification are 3 and the median is 3, and it is finished. It loses ground on craft (a 2243-line monolith, 9-minute suite in 120 root files) and on a thin guard of the default penalty constant, which a seeded mutation exposed (only one test failed). I could not re-run the ruptures cross-check (package not installed), so that 100/100 claim rests on the committed fixtures. Scores are as found on 2026-11-09, before any fix.
